lead: During the window of late 2025 through October 2026, major EFB, flight planning, and crew system vendors—including Jeppesen, Lufthansa Systems, IFS, Aviobook, Bytron Skybook, and Navblue—concentrated their public output on platform updates, artificial intelligence capabilities, and airline customer adoptions. Evidence regarding low-cost carrier (LCC) adoption is insufficient to establish industry concentration with a single competitor, though specific hybrid and LCC instances appear in product launches.

insights.title: Jeppesen and Lufthansa Systems Introduce Advanced Navigation and AI Features
insights.finding: Jeppesen and Lufthansa Systems both released platform enhancements featuring new artificial intelligence and operational capabilities, such as Jeppesen's ForeFlight Airflow AI agents and Lufthansa Systems' Lido mPilot 7.3 taxiway restrictions mapping.
insights.aviation_context: Enhances Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) utility for flight crews navigating complex airport environments and managing flight operations.
insights.caveat: Teasers and initial agent deployments do not confirm full operational rollout across all customer fleets.

insights.title: IFS Secures Multiple EFB Platform Selections Across Regional and Cargo Carriers
insights.finding: IFS expanded its EFB footprint by securing customer selections and deployments for its IFS EFBOne platform with operators including fastjet, TUS Airways, and MY FREIGHTER (Centrum Air).
insights.aviation_context: fastjet operates as a low-cost carrier (LCC) in Africa, TUS Airways as a hybrid/charter carrier, and MY FREIGHTER/Centrum Air as a cargo/hybrid operator.
insights.caveat: Announcements reflect selected or adopted status; ongoing operational performance is not reported.

insights.title: Jeppesen and Lufthansa Systems Capture Major Flag Carrier Implementations
insights.finding: Jeppesen secured a flight planning agreement for Korean Air's integrated fleet and launched Dispatch v2026-2 with Corendon Airlines, while Lufthansa Systems implemented Lido Flight 4D for Kenya Airways.
insights.aviation_context: Korean Air and Kenya Airways are full-service network carriers, while Corendon Airlines is a leisure/LCC carrier.
insights.caveat: Evidence highlights contract agreements and implementations but does not quantify operational efficiency outcomes.

insights.title: Navblue Integrates with Airbus Skywise for Digital Suite Expansion
insights.finding: Navblue merged with Skywise digital solutions to form a new digital services subsidiary and subsequently secured Skywise Digital Suite adoptions with carriers like Pan Am and TransNusa.
insights.aviation_context: Combines flight operations software with broader aircraft health and technical operations data platforms.
insights.caveat: Pan American World Airways represents a restart/return-to-service EIS context rather than an established major network carrier.

insights.title: Insufficient Evidence to Prove LCC Market Concentration with a Single Vendor
insights.finding: While individual low-cost or hybrid carriers like Corendon Airlines adopted Jeppesen and fastjet selected IFS, overall evidence is insufficient to demonstrate that LCC adoption is concentrated with any single competitor.
insights.aviation_context: LCCs typically seek streamlined dispatch and EFB solutions to minimize cockpit workload and ground turnaround times.
insights.caveat: Public capture feeds do not represent exhaustive market share data across all global LCC deployments.

caveat: AI-generated synthesis of captured public signals; verify cited sources before making decisions.
